title: 1 Kings 11
paragraphs: ¹ King Solomon loved many foreign women. In addition to Pharaoh's daughter, he married women from Moab, Ammon, Edom, Sidon, and the Hittites — ² nations about which the LORD had told Israel, "You must not intermarry with them, and they must not marry you, because they will surely turn your heart after their gods." Yet Solomon held fast to these women in love. ³ He had seven hundred wives of royal birth and three hundred concubines — and his wives turned his heart away. ⁴ When Solomon was old, his wives led his heart after other gods, and his heart was no longer fully devoted to the LORD his God, as his father David's heart had been. ⁵ He followed Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, and Molek, the detestable god of the Ammonites.

⁶ Solomon did what was evil in the LORD's sight and did not follow the LORD wholeheartedly, as his father David had done. ⁷ On the hill east of Jerusalem he built a high place for Chemosh, the detestable god of Moab, and for Molek, the detestable god of the Ammonites. ⁸ He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and offered sacrifices to their gods. ⁹ The LORD was angry with Solomon because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice ¹⁰ and had specifically warned him about worshipping other gods — but Solomon had not obeyed.

¹¹ So the LORD said to Solomon: "Since this is how you have behaved — since you have not kept my covenant and my decrees, which I commanded you — I will certainly tear the kingdom away from you and give it to one of your servants. ¹² Nevertheless, for the sake of your father David, I will not do it during your lifetime. I will tear it from your son's hand. ¹³ Yet I will not tear the whole kingdom away. For the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen, I will give your son one tribe." ¹⁴ Then the LORD raised up an adversary against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite, who was of the royal line of Edom. ¹⁵ Earlier, when David was fighting in Edom, Joab the commander of the army had gone to bury the dead and had struck down every male in Edom.

¹⁶ (For six months Joab had remained there with all Israel, until he had cut off every male in Edom.) ¹⁷ So Hadad had fled to Egypt — he and certain Edomite servants of his father's household — Hadad being just a small child at the time. ¹⁸ They set out from Midian and came to Paran, where they gathered some men and went on to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt. Pharaoh gave Hadad a house, assigned him provisions, and granted him land. ¹⁹ Pharaoh was so pleased with Hadad that he gave him the sister of his own wife — the sister of Queen Tahpenes — in marriage. ²⁰ The sister of Tahpenes bore him a son named Genubath, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh's palace; and Genubath lived in Pharaoh's household among Pharaoh's own sons.

²¹ When Hadad heard in Egypt that David had died and that Joab the commander of the army was also dead, he said to Pharaoh, "Let me go back to my own country." ²² Pharaoh asked him, "But what have you lacked here with me, that you want to leave?" "Nothing," Hadad replied, "but please let me go." ²³ God also raised up against Solomon another adversary: Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from his master Hadadezer king of Zobah. ²⁴ After David had destroyed Zobah's forces, Rezon gathered men around himself and became leader of a band of raiders. They went to Damascus, settled there, and set up their rule in Damascus. ²⁵ Rezon was an adversary to Israel throughout Solomon's lifetime, adding to the trouble that Hadad caused. He despised Israel and reigned over Aram.

²⁶ Then there was Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephrathite from Zereda — one of Solomon's officials, whose mother was a widow named Zeruah — and he too rebelled against the king. ²⁷ This is the account of how he came to rebel: Solomon had built the Millo and had closed up the gap in the wall of the city of David his father. ²⁸ Jeroboam was a man of ability, and Solomon saw how hard he worked and put him in charge of the whole labor force of the house of Joseph. ²⁹ About that time Jeroboam was going out of Jerusalem, and the prophet Ahijah of Shiloh met him on the road. Ahijah was wearing a new cloak, and the two of them were out in the country alone. ³⁰ Ahijah took hold of his new cloak and tore it into twelve pieces.

³¹ He said to Jeroboam, "Take ten pieces for yourself — for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I am about to tear the kingdom out of Solomon's hand and give you ten tribes. ³² But one tribe will remain his, for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel — ³³ because they have forsaken me and worshiped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites. They have not walked in my ways and done what is right in my eyes, nor kept my decrees and laws as David, Solomon's father, did. ³⁴ But I will not take the whole kingdom from him. I will keep him ruler all the days of his life for the sake of my servant David, whom I chose and who kept my commands and decrees. ³⁵ But I will take the kingdom from his son's hands and give you ten of the tribes.

³⁶ I will give one tribe to his son so that David my servant may always have a lamp before me in Jerusalem, the city where I chose to put my Name. ³⁷ I will take you, and you will rule over all that your heart desires; you will be king over Israel. ³⁸ If you do whatever I command you and walk in my ways and do what is right in my eyes — keeping my decrees and commands as my servant David did — I will be with you. I will build you a dynasty as enduring as the one I built for David, and I will give Israel to you. ³⁹ I will humble David's descendants because of this, though not forever." ⁴⁰ Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam fled to Egypt, to Shishak the king, and stayed there until Solomon's death.

⁴¹ As for the rest of the acts of Solomon — all he did and his wisdom — are they not written in the book of the annals of Solomon? ⁴² Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years. ⁴³ Then he died and was buried in the city of David his father, and his son Rehoboam succeeded him as king.
